title: Multiplication Table (Practicing Multiplication with Chosen Numbers)

text.text:
#### Practicing Multiplication with Chosen Numbers

Choose the number to be multiplied and the one-digit number in the fields above the multiplication. The number can have one, two or three digits, and the multiplication is written vertically and solved column by column, from the units.

- The light blue squares are the ones carried from the previous order; the neutral squares are the product of the column.
- Type the digit that stays in the column in the box on the result row.
- When the column reaches ten or more, a carry box appears above the next order: type the number of complete groups of ten in it.

The values are checked as you type: a wrong value colours the squares and shows a tip; the right values fill them, show a congratulation and the button for the next column.

**Example: 7 × 8.** The group of 7 squares is repeated eight times: 7 × 8 = 56. Five complete groups of ten are carried to the next order and 6 squares stay outside — that is the digit 6. Type 6 in the result row and 5 in the carry box.

#### The Game

Choose the number and the one-digit number above the multiplication, then type the digit that stays in the column and, when it reaches ten or more, the carry above the next order.
